result.title: Polarity--Time Interaction and Multi-Level Reliability for Event-Based Spacecraft Pose Estimation
result.summary: Sparse event responses produce uneven keypoint errors whose effects on spacecraft pose depend on correspondence geometry and the reliability of successive observations. We present a reliability-aware framework connecting polarity--time localization, geometric recovery, event--CAD refinement, and trajectory optimization. A three-branch representation combines positive events, negative events, and recent-event timing through cross-branch attention and gating, followed by spatiotemporal aggregation. An ordered semantic-point head estimates relative correspondence precision for geometrically constrained pose recovery. Event-edge and CAD-projection agreement then guide local pose refinement under keypoint-geometry safeguards. At the sequence level, a ten-dimensional descriptor combines heatmap shape, reprojection consistency, and geometric conditioning to set time-aligned observation scales. On the official SPADES challenge test set, the complete system achieves a combined pose score of 0.0474, approximately 5.4\% below PASAN+IRIS. Validation ablations reduce the score from 0.0772 for base localization with uniform PnP to 0.0514 for the complete cascade; on identical single-frame observations, quality weighting reduces the score from 0.0549 with constant-weight optimization to 0.0514.

AI.brief_summary: 提出面向事件相机航天器位姿估计的可靠性感知框架：用正事件、负事件与时间近因三分支表示定位关键点并估计对应精度，结合事件边缘与 CAD 投影一致性做局部位姿精化，并在序列层面用十维描述子调节各观测的权重。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按对应关系可靠性加权几何求解、并以描述子为连续多次观测定权的做法，可能为 LVR 中的视觉证据筛选、多步观测贡献分配与置信度门控提供可供核查的线索，但领域与推理状态生成相距较远。
